cards.name: Katniss Everdeen
cards.summary: Katniss Everdeen is the main protagonist and narrator of The Hunger Games trilogy. After her younger sister, Primrose Everdeen, was reaped in the 74th Hunger Games, Katniss volunteered to take her place as the female tribute from District 12. This action set in motion the events of the entire series. She is the…

cards.name: Peeta Mellark
cards.summary: Peeta Mellark, a baker's son from District 12, is the deuteragonist of The Hunger Games trilogy. He was reaped alongside Katniss Everdeen for the 74th Hunger Games. He and Katniss play out in the arena in order to garner sponsors and manage to both become victors by tricking the Gamemakers. Although his feelings…

cards.name: Haymitch Abernathy
cards.summary: Haymitch Abernathy was District 12's second and only living Hunger Games victor for 23 years, having won the second Quarter Quell before Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark won the 74th Hunger Games under his mentorship. He worked secretly in tandem with District 13 and other victors in order to incite the Second…

cards.name: Coriolanus Snow
cards.summary: Coriolanus Snow was a totalitarian autocrat who ruled as the tyrannical President of Panem for more than two decades. In his youth, he was known by the nickname Coryo, originally given to him by his cousin, Tigris.

cards.name: Finnick Odair
cards.summary: Finnick Odair was a male Career victor from District 4 who won the 65th Hunger Games at 14, making him the youngest victor in Hunger Games history. Known for his charm, exceptional skill with a trident, and popularity among Capitol citizens over his good looks, Finnick became a prominent victor in Panem in the…

cards.name: District 12
cards.summary: District 12 was the smallest and poorest of the thirteen districts of Panem. Located in Appalachia, it had a population of around 8,000 people prior to being firebombed by the Capitol. District 12's main industry is coal mining, but after the Second Rebellion, their main industry was converted to medicine. District…

cards.name: Gale Hawthorne
cards.summary: Gale Hawthorne was Katniss Everdeen's best friend and hunting partner, and one of the main characters of the trilogy. He is fiercely devoted to his family, to Katniss, and to the rebel cause. He is in love with Katniss and is forced to watch as she volunteers for the 74th Hunger Games in the place of her sister and…

cards.name: The Capitol
cards.summary: The Capitol of Panem is a technologically advanced metropolis and home to the nation's elite. The Capitol is also the colloquial name for the ruling regime of Panem. As the supreme seat of authority in the country, this city rules the nation's thirteen districts (twelve after the Dark Days). The Hunger Games are…

cards.name: Effie Trinket
cards.summary: Effie Trinket is the escort for the District 12 tributes, acting as an advisor to Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark, while she accompanies them to the Capitol and various other activities. She also acted as a stylist and escort for Haymitch Abernathy for his Games. After the Second Rebellion, she is the only…

cards.name: Primrose Everdeen
cards.summary: Primrose "Prim" Everdeen was Katniss Everdeen's younger sister and Burdock and Asterid Everdeen's youngest daughter. She grew up in the Seam, the poorest section of District 12, and had two pets: a cat named Buttercup and a goat named Lady.

cards.name: Cato
cards.summary: Cato is the secondary antagonist of The Hunger Games. He was the male tribute from District 2 in the 74th Hunger Games. He was the leader of the Career Tributes' alliance, the strongest tribute in the arena, and Katniss Everdeen's primary adversary.

cards.name: District 13
cards.summary: District 13 is one of the thirteen districts of Panem, and for a 75-year period between the Dark Days and Second Rebellion, an independent nation. Located in far northeastern part of the country, District 13 was widely thought to have been destroyed by the Capitol in the Dark Days, 74 years before The Hunger Games…

cards.name: Cinna
cards.summary: Cinna was Katniss Everdeen's stylist during her campaigns in the 74th and 75th Hunger Games, who was later revealed to be a supporter of the rebels in District 13. Cinna played a major role in Katniss' rise to prominence in the rebel movement and with her political persona as the Mockingjay.

cards.name: Rue
cards.summary: Rue was the 12-year-old female tribute from District 11 who was selected to participate in the 74th Hunger Games. Rue formed an alliance with Katniss Everdeen after warning her about a nest of tracker jackers. Rue decided to trust Katniss partly because of the pin she wore over her heart: the famous mockingjay pin.…

cards.name: Johanna Mason
cards.summary: Johanna Mason of District 7 was the victor of the 71st Hunger Games. Four years later, she became a tribute in the third Quarter Quell, and she was a prisoner of war in the Second Rebellion. She was the last living victor from District 7 by the end of the rebellion.

cards.name: Career Tribute
cards.summary: Career Tributes, commonly known as Careers, were tributes who trained from a young age to compete in the Hunger Games. They attended specialized combat academies in their districts, where they were instructed by prior victors and skilled trainers, until they turned 18 - the age at which Careers usually would…

cards.name: Tribute
cards.summary: Tributes were residents of Panem's twelve districts who were reaped or volunteered to participate in the annual Hunger Games. Except in special cases such as Quarter Quells, 24 children between the ages of 12 and 18 were chosen at random to participate. Every district had to send one girl and one boy to the…

cards.name: Thresh
cards.summary: Thresh was the male tribute from District 11 in the 74th Hunger Games. During the Games, he killed Clove and spared Katniss Everdeen's life.

cards.name: Plutarch Heavensbee
cards.summary: Plutarch Heavensbee is the Head Gamemaker for the 75th Hunger Games, taking the place of Seneca Crane. A secret rebel-insider, he becomes a commander of the rebel forces of District 13 during the Second Rebellion.

cards.name: Lucy Gray Baird
cards.summary: Lucy Gray Baird was a female tribute from District 12, a Capitol favorite, and the eventual victor of the 10th Hunger Games. Her mentor was Coriolanus Snow, a top-performing student at the Academy who developed feelings for her along the way.

cards.name: Maysilee Donner
cards.summary: Maysilee Donner was one of the female tributes from District 12 in the 50th Hunger Games, also known as the second Quarter Quell. She placed 4th out of 48 in her Games and was an ally of Haymitch Abernathy. She was the daughter of Mr. and Mrs. Donner. She was Merrilee Undersee's twin sister and Madge Undersee's…

cards.name: Beetee Latier
cards.summary: Beetee Latier, nicknamed “Volts,” is a male tribute from District 3.

cards.name: Clove
cards.summary: Clove is the tertiary antagonist of The Hunger Games. She was the female tribute from District 2 in the 74th Hunger Games. A ruthless, sadistic, and highly skilled Career Tribute, Clove became one of Katniss Everdeen's main adversaries in the arena. She was incredibly skilled with knives and could throw them with…

cards.name: Marvel
cards.summary: Marvel is a minor antagonist in The Hunger Games. He was the male tribute from District 1 in the 74th Hunger Games and a member of the Career pack.

cards.name: Glimmer
cards.summary: Glimmer was the female tribute from District 1 in the 74th Hunger Games. Along with her district partner, Marvel, she was a member of the "Career pack" that banded together to hunt down the weaker competitors. She was indirectly killed by Katniss Everdeen, who dropped a nest of tracker jackers on the Career pack as…

cards.name: District 2
cards.summary: District 2 is one of the thirteen districts of Panem. Landlocked and located in the Rocky Mountains, extremely close to the Capitol itself, it is one of the largest and wealthiest districts. Publicly, District 2 is presented solely as the home of the nation's stone quarries and masonry workers, but it is also where…

cards.name: District 11
cards.summary: District 11 is one of the thirteen districts of Panem. Its main industry is agriculture.

cards.name: Peacekeepers
cards.summary: Peacekeepers, also called Peacemakers, comprise a paramilitary gendarmerie which was controlled by the Capitol, and tasked with maintaining order throughout the nation of Panem. Led by a Head Peacekeeper who is the commander of the garrison of a district, they are the primary instrument of control and repression…

cards.name: Wiress
cards.summary: Wiress of District 3 was the victor of the 49th Hunger Games. Known for her odd demeanor and eccentricities, similar in nature to her fellow victor and district colleague Beetee Latier, she was relatively well known for her nickname "Nuts". A woman of impressive intellect, Wiress mentored many tributes over the…

cards.name: Caesar Flickerman
cards.summary: Caesar Flickerman was the last host for the Hunger Games, responsible for interviewing tributes the night before the competition began.

cards.name: Annie Cresta
cards.summary: Annie Cresta is a Career victor from District 4 known for winning the 70th Hunger Games. She is the widow of Finnick Odair and the mother of their son.

cards.name: Tigris
cards.summary: Tigris was a former Hunger Games stylist , fashion designer and Capitol rebel who played a significant role in the events surrounding the 10th Hunger Games and the Second Rebellion. Born into the once-wealthy Snow family, she was the elder cousin of Coriolanus Snow, the future president of Panem, with whom she…

cards.name: Mags Flanagan
cards.summary: Mags Flanagan was the female tribute from District 4 during the 75th Hunger Games, for which she volunteered in place of Annie Cresta. She was also the victor of the 11th Hunger Games. She was also the mentor for victors Haymitch Abernathy during the 50th Hunger Games and Finnick Odair during the 65th Hunger Games.

cards.name: Muttation
cards.summary: Muttations, or simply mutts, are genetically modified animals created by the Capitol for use as weapons, both in conflicts against rebels and within Hunger Games arenas.

cards.name: Sejanus Plinth
cards.summary: Sejanus Plinth was a Capitol citizen, formerly from District 2, and mentor of the male tribute of District 2, Marcus, during the 10th Hunger Games. Marcus was formerly a childhood friend of Sejanus and he was quite eager for Marcus to win. He was one of the 24 top-performing seniors of the Academy selected for a…

cards.name: Enobaria
cards.summary: Enobaria is a female Career Tribute from District 2 and the victor of the 62nd Hunger Games. She competed again in the Third Quarter Quell against other victors.

cards.name: Alma Coin
cards.summary: Alma Coin was the President of District 13 and a leader in the Second Rebellion. She orchestrated the City Circle bombing, clearing the way for her to become the interim President of Panem, before she was assassinated by Katniss Everdeen. Coin is the hidden secondary antagonist in the book Mockingjay.

cards.name: District 4
cards.summary: District 4 is one of Panem's wealthiest districts. Its major industry is fishing, and children are trained for jobs in this industry from a young age.

cards.name: District 1
cards.summary: District 1 is the wealthiest district in Panem, whose primary industry is the manufacture of luxury items for the Capitol. As a result, District 1 has a generally favorable relationship with the Capitol, although they are still forced to participate in the annual Hunger Games like all the other districts. However,…

cards.name: Wyatt Callow
cards.summary: Wyatt Callow was one of the two male tributes from District 12 who participated in the 50th Hunger Games. He was the son of the late Jethro Callow.

cards.name: Asterid Everdeen
cards.summary: Asterid Everdeen (née March) is the mother of Katniss and Primrose Everdeen and the wife of the deceased Burdock Everdeen.

cards.name: Arena
cards.summary: An arena is a large, enclosed, outdoor area where the Hunger Games were held each year. Arenas were designed by the Gamemakers and a new one was built every year. It could be anything from dense forest to an open meadow, or a frozen wasteland to a scorched desert. The Gamemakers planted traps and introduced cunning…

cards.name: District 8
cards.summary: District 8 is one of the thirteen districts of Panem. Its main industry is textile production. They have at least one factory that is used for making Peacekeeper uniforms.

cards.name: District 3
cards.summary: District 3 is one of the 13 districts of Panem. Its main industry is technology, and people manufacture televisions, computers, and other electronics.

cards.name: Cashmere
cards.summary: Cashmere was a victor from District 1 who won the 64th Hunger Games. She was also a tribute in the 75th Hunger Games (also known as the third Quarter Quell).

cards.name: District 9
cards.summary: District 9 is one of Panem's thirteen districts, and its primary industry is grain production. It was known to have poor education and long hours in the grain fields.

cards.name: Seneca Crane
cards.summary: Seneca Crane was the Head Gamemaker of the 72nd, 73rd, and 74th Hunger Games, in charge of coordinating game play and ordering the creation of obstacles into the arena. At the end of the 74th Games, he allowed both Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark to emerge as victors, rather than allow them to commit suicide and…

cards.name: Lenore Dove Baird
cards.summary: Lenore Dove Baird was a Covey girl from District 12 who was dating Haymitch Abernathy.

cards.name: Covey
cards.summary: The Covey were a nomadic people in Panem known for their musical talent and performances.

cards.name: Volumnia Gaul
cards.summary: Volumnia Gaul, usually known as Dr. Gaul, was Head Gamemaker and the overseer of every Hunger Games since their inception, at least up to and including the 10th Hunger Games. She was also a professor of military theory at the University and head of the Capitol's Experimental Weapons Division, based at the Citadel…

cards.name: Madge Undersee
cards.summary: Madge Undersee was the daughter of District 12's Mayor Undersee, and she was a friend of Katniss Everdeen's from school.

cards.name: Cornucopia
cards.summary: The Cornucopia was a large metal structure that served as the starting point for 50 Hunger Games arenas.

cards.name: District 7
cards.summary: District 7 is one of the thirteen districts of Panem. It provided lumber and paper to the Capitol.

cards.name: Victor
cards.summary: Victors are tributes who have won previous Hunger Games. Because of this, they receive income from the Capitol for life, are given a special status in their districts, and are allowed to live in the wealthiest part of their district called the Victors' Village with their families. Despite the privileges they enjoy,…

cards.name: Burdock Everdeen
cards.summary: Burdock Everdeen, nicknamed "Burdie" by Haymitch Abernathy, was the father of Katniss and Primrose Everdeen, as well as being Asterid Everdeen's husband. He lived and worked inside the gates of District 12 as a coal miner, poacher, and Katniss's teacher when it came to hunting in the woods, singing, and making good…

cards.name: District 5
cards.summary: District 5 is one of the thirteen districts of Panem. Its main industry is power and utility, and the district is responsible for generating the power of the entire nation.

cards.name: Proserpina Trinket
cards.summary: Proserpina "Prosie" Trinket was a Capitol University student who was a member of the prep team for Haymitch Abernathy during the 50th Hunger Games. She was Effie Trinket's younger sister. She studied fashion and styling, with an explicit focus on tribute presentation. She and Vitus, her fellow underclassman and…

cards.name: Gloss
cards.summary: Gloss was the male District 1 victor of the 63rd Hunger Games. He also participated as a Career Tribute in the 75th Hunger Games, also known as the third Quarter Quell.

cards.name: District 10
cards.summary: District 10 is one of Panem's thirteen districts. Its main industry is livestock, and it provides meat to the Capitol.

cards.name: District 6
cards.summary: District 6 is one of the thirteen districts of Panem, whose principal industry is transportation.

cards.name: Lou Lou
cards.summary: "Lou Lou" was a body double for Louella McCoy, one of the female tributes from District 12, following her death during the chariot rides. She ultimately participated and died in the 50th Hunger Games.

cards.name: Training Center
cards.summary: The Training Center, also known as the Tribute Center, is a building located in the middle of the Capitol, just behind the president's mansion on the City Circle. Upon arriving to the city in preparation for the Hunger Games, it is where tributes live and train. The center has an open roof, which includes a garden…

cards.name: Buttercup
cards.summary: Buttercup was a "hideous-looking cat" that belonged to Primrose Everdeen. He later came into the ownership of Prim's older sister, Katniss Everdeen.

cards.name: Brutus
cards.summary: Brutus was the male tribute from District 2 for the 75th Hunger Games, and the victor of an unknown past Games, presumably in the mid to late 40s. He was also a Career Tribute.

cards.name: Wellie
cards.summary: Wellie was one of two female tributes from District 6 who participated in the 50th Hunger Games.

cards.name: Reaper Ash
cards.summary: Reaper Ash was the male tribute from District 11 in the 10th Hunger Games. His mentor was Clemensia Dovecote.

cards.name: Casca Highbottom
cards.summary: Casca Highbottom was the Dean of the Academy and the unintentional creator of the Hunger Games. When the creation of the games was officially announced, Highbottom served as the public face of the event, beginning a years-long downward spiral that would end with his assassination by future president Coriolanus Snow.

cards.name: Clemensia Dovecote
cards.summary: Clemensia Dovecote was a female resident of the Capitol and a student of the Academy. She was one of 24 top-performing seniors at the Academy selected to be a mentor for the 10th Hunger Games. She was assigned the male tribute from District 11, Reaper Ash.

cards.name: Ampert Latier
cards.summary: Ampert Latier was one of the two male tributes from District 3 who participated in the 50th Hunger Games. He is the son of the District 3 victor Beetee Latier.

cards.name: Drusilla Sickle
cards.summary: Drusilla Sickle is the escort for the District 12 tributes during the 50th Hunger Games.

cards.name: Coral
cards.summary: Coral was the female tribute from District 4 during the 10th Hunger Games. Her mentor was Festus Creed. Coral finished 6th in the Games. She was preceded in death by the District 3 male Circ and succeeded by her district partner Mizzen. She was in an alliance with Mizzen and Tanner, the male tribute from District…

cards.name: Bow and arrow
cards.summary: The bow and arrow is a projectile weapon that predates recorded history and is common to most cultures. Archery is the art, practice, or skill of using the weapon. Katniss Everdeen learned her archery skills from her father and used a bow to hunt for food in the woods outside of District 12. The bow also became her…

cards.name: The Newcomers
cards.summary: The Newcomers were an alliance of tributes formed by Ampert to build an alliance to rival the Career Pack during the 50th Hunger Games. Ampert hoped this would even out the odds and combat the hunting tactics used by Careers. A number of them were also rebels involved in a plot to disrupt the Hunger Games. The…

cards.name: Tam Amber
cards.summary: Tam Amber was a resident of District 12 and a member of the Covey. Tam Amber was a standout player on his mandolin, performing with lightning-fast fingering while keeping his facial features expressionless and distant.

cards.name: Chaff
cards.summary: Chaff was the male tribute for District 11 who participated in the 75th Hunger Games and was the victor of the 45th Hunger Games.

cards.name: Tracker jacker
cards.summary: Tracker jackers are genetically engineered wasp muttations, designed and invented by the Capitol. They exist only as a conception of the sadistic tendencies of Panem's dictators. They are genetically programmed to attack anyone or anything that disturbs their hive. They follow their targets far away from their…

cards.name: Silka Sharp
cards.summary: Silka Sharp was a Career Tribute from District 1 who participated in the 50th Hunger Games. She was a part of the Career alliance, and she placed 2nd out of 48 tributes.

cards.name: Mizzen
cards.summary: Mizzen was the male tribute from District 4 during the 10th Hunger Games. He finished in 5th place of the 24 tributes. He was preceded in death by his district partner Coral and followed by the female tribute from District 3, Teslee. His mentor was Persephone Price. He was in an alliance with Coral and the male…

cards.name: Portia
cards.summary: Portia was Peeta Mellark's stylist for the 74th and 75th Hunger Games.

cards.name: Lyme
cards.summary: Lyme was a victor of an unspecified edition of the Hunger Games from District 2 and a commander in the Second Rebellion against the Capitol.

cards.name: Clerk Carmine Clade
cards.summary: Clerk Carmine Clade, sometimes known as CC, was a member of the Covey, and he played the fiddle in their band. He was the younger brother of Billy Taupe Clade, and later in life, he was one of Lenore Dove Baird's guardians.

cards.name: Victors' Village
cards.summary: The Victors' Village is a wealthy neighborhood in every district where past victors of the Hunger Games reside. They contain at least twelve luxurious houses which are given to victors as rewards for surviving the Hunger Games. When the victor dies, everyone sharing the house with them must leave and move back to…

cards.name: Lamina
cards.summary: Lamina was the female tribute reaped from District 7 during the 10th Hunger Games. She died on the third day of the Games and finished in 10th place of the 24 tributes (though only 15 tributes made it to the start of Day 1 of these Games). She was one of the few tributes to not be in a known direct alliance with…

cards.name: Academy
cards.summary: The Academy was an elite, four-year secondary school in the Capitol for the children of the wealthy and powerful.

cards.name: Mockingjay (bird)
cards.summary: The mockingjay is a bird that was created through the unintended mating of mockingbirds and jabberjays.

cards.name: The Seam
cards.summary: Coal dust covered everything in the Seam, including the streets, houses, and even the people themselves. Residents of the Seam lived in "squat gray houses" with a number of gates, yards, and alleys between them.

cards.name: Avox
cards.summary: An Avox is a mute servant who had their tongue cut out in lieu of execution as a punishment for being a rebel, traitor, deserter or criminal. They spent their lives as the lowest class in Panem, permanently serving the Capitol as slaves.

cards.name: Louella McCoy
cards.summary: Louella McCoy was one of the two female tributes from District 12 chosen during the reaping to participate in the 50th Hunger Games.

cards.name: Blight
cards.summary: Blight was the male tribute from District 7 who participated in the 75th Hunger Games. He was also the victor of an unspecified Hunger Games.

cards.name: Jessup Diggs
cards.summary: Jessup Diggs was the male tribute from District 12 in the 10th Hunger Games. His mentor was Lysistrata Vickers. He became the ally of Lucy Gray Baird for the Games.

cards.name: Panache Barker
cards.summary: Panache Barker was one of two male Career Tributes from District 1 who participated in the 50th Hunger Games. He was related to Palladium Barker, the victor of the 46th Hunger Games.

cards.name: Boggs
cards.summary: Boggs was President Coin's second-in-command. Boggs' rank was colonel and he was Head of Security of District 13. When Katniss Everdeen assumed the role of the Mockingjay, he became her protector.

cards.name: Training stations
cards.summary: There are many different training stations inside the gymnasium of the Training Center where tributes could learn and practice skills that helped them survive in the Hunger Games arena. These skills included training with many types of weapons, as well as survival techniques, like setting traps and recognizing…

cards.name: Seeder
cards.summary: Seeder was the female tribute from District 11 in the 75th Hunger Games, and she was the victor of an unspecified Hunger Games.

cards.name: Rebels
cards.summary: The term "rebels" refers to individuals who challenge the authority of the Capitol, especially through armed insurrection. This term is used frequently throughout the trilogy by various individuals, including President Snow, Capitol officials, and the rebels themselves. The rebel army was composed of militia…

cards.name: Cecelia
cards.summary: Cecelia was the District 8 female tribute who participated in the 75th Hunger Games. She was also the victor of an unspecified Hunger Games.

cards.name: Lysistrata Vickers
cards.summary: Lysistrata Vickers, also known as Lyssie, was a female resident of the Capitol and a student of the Academy. She was one of 24 top-performing seniors at the Academy selected to be a mentor for the 10th Hunger Games.

cards.name: Treech
cards.summary: Treech was the male tribute from District 7 in the 10th Hunger Games. His mentor was Vipsania Sickle.

cards.name: Grandma'am
cards.summary: The Grandma'am is the grandmother of Coriolanus Snow and Tigris. Her nickname was created by a young Tigris, who felt she deserved an imperial name.

cards.name: Bobbin
cards.summary: Bobbin was the male tribute from District 8 reaped for the 10th Hunger Games. His mentor was Juno Phipps. During his interview with Phipps, he impressed the public by explaining five different ways to kill someone with a sewing needle. He died during the night of Day 1 and finished in 13th place of the 24 tributes.…

cards.name: Tanner
cards.summary: Tanner was the male tribute from District 10 in the 10th Hunger Games. His mentor was Domitia Whimsiwick. For a short amount of time, he was in an alliance with the District 4 duo, Mizzen and Coral.

cards.name: Morphlings
cards.summary: The morphlings were two tributes from District 6, one male and one female. They each won a previous unknown Hunger Games and participated in the 75th Hunger Games. As victors, they were likely given the responsibility of mentoring other tributes from District 6.

cards.name: Arachne Crane
cards.summary: Arachne Crane was a female resident of the Capitol and a student of the Academy. She was one of 24 top-performing seniors at the Academy selected to be a mentor for the 10th Hunger Games. She was assigned the female tribute from District 10, Brandy.

cards.name: Hovercraft
cards.summary: A hovercraft is a type of aircraft used in Panem, mainly by the Capitol, but is later also used by members of the rebellion. They serve a variety of roles from supporting the Hunger Games to transportation and combat. They are manufactured in District 6.

cards.name: Kerna
cards.summary: Kerna was one of two female tributes from District 9 who participated in the 50th Hunger Games.

cards.name: Cressida
cards.summary: Cressida is a resident of the Capitol and a film director who defected to the rebellion along with her camera crew (Castor and Pollux), and her assistant Messalla. They headed to District 13 when they fled the Capitol. Cressida was tasked by Plutarch Heavensbee with following Katniss Everdeen throughout her…

cards.name: Merrilee Undersee
cards.summary: Merrilee Undersee (née Donner) was the daughter of Mr. and Mrs. Donner. She was Maysilee Donner's twin sister who was one of the female tributes for District 12 in the 50th Hunger Games. She was Mayor Undersee's wife and Madge Undersee's mother. She lived in District 12 with her family.

cards.name: Claudius Templesmith
cards.summary: Claudius Templesmith was the announcer of the Hunger Games. He had a deep, booming voice.

cards.name: Jabberjay
cards.summary: A jabberjay is an exclusively male bird muttation created in the Capitol by Dr. Kay to spy on enemies of the Capitol. Jabberjays had the ability to memorize and repeat entire human conversations.

cards.name: Festus Creed
cards.summary: Festus Creed was a male resident of the Capitol and a student of the Academy. He was one of 24 top-performing seniors at the Academy selected to be a mentor for the 10th Hunger Games. He was assigned the female tribute from District 4, Coral.

cards.name: Capitol Arena
cards.summary: The Capitol Arena was a dilapidated amphitheater in the Capitol that was later appropriated as the first Hunger Games arena. The 1st through 10th Hunger Games were held there. After the 10th Hunger Games, the arena was abandoned and the Gamemakers began using existing settings in the wild or bombed-out towns and…

cards.name: The Hob
cards.summary: The Hob was District 12's black market. It was the only place to buy and sell illegal goods like liquor and poached game. It was often open at times when most legal stores would not be, such as on the day of the reaping.

cards.name: Pod
cards.summary: A pod is an obstacle or weapon designed to trap or kill anyone in proximity of its activation. The Capitol planted many pods around the city, which served in its defense during the Second Rebellion.

cards.name: Justice Building
cards.summary: The Justice Building is a place in each of Panem's districts where official business is conducted.

cards.name: Train
cards.summary: Trains are the primary method of travel throughout Panem. They are mainly reserved for the shipment of one district's goods and materials to another, and for the transportation of Capitol officials. Most of Panem's citizens are not authorized to travel by train unless they are reaped for the Hunger Games, as travel…

cards.name: Nightlock
cards.summary: Nightlock is a wild plant with extremely poisonous berries. Katniss first heard about this plant from her father, who cautioned her that anyone who ate nightlock would be dead before the berries even reached their stomach. Although this phrasing may be an exaggeration, the plant's effects are indisputable: Foxface…

cards.name: Fire
cards.summary: Fire is an important motif that reappears throughout The Hunger Games trilogy.

cards.name: Force field
cards.summary: Force fields are invisible electric fields set up by the Capitol that are used to prevent tributes from escaping the arena and any other places so they won't run away from the Games. It tosses anything that hits it back to where it was before, so tributes couldn't commit suicide by jumping off the roof of the…

cards.name: Wolf mutt
cards.summary: The wolf mutts were muttations set loose on the tributes in the 74th Hunger Games.

cards.name: Capitol TV
cards.summary: Capitol TV is the main television network within the Capitol. It was used for promotional purposes in regards to the film The Hunger Games: Mockingjay - Part 1, where President Snow addressed the nation of Panem. The TV network was also known for broadcasting the Hunger Games.

cards.name: Lizard mutt
cards.summary: The lizard mutts were reptilian muttations that were used against rebels during the Battle of the Capitol.

cards.name: Snake mutt
cards.summary: The snake mutts were muttations used during the 10th Hunger Games.

cards.name: Capitol News
cards.summary: Capitol News was an organization which covered the news in and of interest to the Capitol, along with Capitol TV. Their coverage was said to be omnipresent. Typically, the news would cover the weather, local news, and small things such as recipes.

cards.name: Drone
cards.summary: A drone is a small flying device used to deliver sponsor gifts to tributes during the Hunger Games. They were first used in the 10th Hunger Games.

cards.name: Monkey mutt
cards.summary: The monkey mutts were primate muttations used in the 75th Hunger Games.

cards.name: Communicuff
cards.summary: A communicuff was a piece of technology used in the Capitol and District 13.

cards.name: Tracker
cards.summary: A tracker is a small piece of technology used by the Gamemakers to locate each tribute inside the Hunger Games arena.

cards.name: Sunflower bomb
cards.summary: The sunflower bomb was an explosive created by Beetee Latier for the rebel plot to disrupt the 50th Hunger Games.

cards.name: Holo
cards.summary: A Holo is a handheld device used by the rebels to show locations of known pods hidden in the Capitol streets.

cards.name: Domesticated animals
cards.summary: A list of domesticated animals referenced in The Hunger Games series, not including muttations or wildlife.

cards.name: Fog
cards.summary: This type of fog was a poisonous, corrosive vapor released by the Gamemakers in the 75th Hunger Games arena as one of the hourly horrors. cards.name: Nuclear weaponry
cards.summary: The nuclear weaponry of Panem was centered in District 13. The country's nuclear arsenal was presumably a large one, as they dedicated an entire district to it. There was also a nuclear arsenal in the west.

cards.name: Tribute tube
cards.summary: Tribute tubes were glass cylinders that facilitated Hunger Games tributes' transport into the arena.
